bug_semantics: The GET /conversions/get_history_details?history_id=<id> handler loads a retained ConversionHistory row and serializes input_text, old_output_text, and new_output_text. A soft-deleted conversion is hidden by the normal conversion lookup, so the lookup returns None. The pre-fix authorization condition was guarded by the conversion object's truthiness; None therefore skipped the visibility denial and the handler returned the history payload. An attacker able to identify or enumerate a history id could read the deleted conversion's retained input/output. Before the later login gate this endpoint was anonymous; after that gate the deleted-parent case still succeeded for any authenticated requester who could supply the id.
flaw_origin: Commit bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34 changed conversion deletion from db.session.delete(convert) to a soft delete (is_active=False plus deleted_at), retaining the associated history rows while an already-existing history-details endpoint returned those rows by id without authorization. Its immediate follow-up 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a attempted to secure the endpoint but simultaneously made the normal lookup hide inactive conversions and used `if convert_obj and ...`, preserving the disclosure specifically for the newly retained deleted-parent state. Later persistence moves and authorization-predicate refactors preserved the same fail-open semantics; they are not introducers.
evidence: The first-party GitHub advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9p5q-96wv-4xvh describes the incomplete authorization check: a deleted conversion lookup returns None, the prior logic denied only when the object existed and visibility failed, and retained history input/output was disclosed. It references fix commit 88dc65f0117cf7a120f6252674c529e7b9c9b8c3; the advisory itself lists affected and patched versions as Unknown.

Run `git show bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34 -- website/web/convert/convert_core.py website/web/convert/convert.py`. In convert_core.py, delete_convert changes from deleting and committing the Conversion row to setting is_active=False and deleted_at, and the commit adds restore/hard-delete/trash operations. At the same commit, website/web/convert/convert.py:get_history_details still fetches a history row directly and returns history.to_json() without checking the parent conversion or caller visibility. This is the first commit at which ordinary deletion retains a history row that this endpoint can disclose.

Direct-parent check: `git grep -n -A14 -B3 'def delete_convert' 3e456f1d952e564965feafd370ab030826cf3f47 -- website/web/convert/convert_core.py` shows db.session.delete(convert) and commit, while `website/db_class/db.py` declares ConvertHistory.convert_id with ForeignKey('convert.id', ondelete='CASCADE'). Thus the parent lacks the soft-deleted-parent/retained-history state. `git grep -n -A18 -B4 'def get_history_details' 3e456f1d952e564965feafd370ab030826cf3f47 -- website/web/convert/convert.py` confirms the endpoint existed, but deletion removed the referenced conversion rather than retaining it inactive.

Run `git show 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a -- website/web/convert/convert.py website/web/convert/convert_core.py`. The follow-up adds @login_required and the guard `if convert_obj and not convert_obj.public`, while get_convert changes to return None for !is_active unless include_deleted=True. This turns the pre-existing broad missing-authorization exposure into the exact advisory fail-open: the deleted lookup is None, so the guarded denial is skipped.

Run `git log -L :get_history_details:website/web/conversions/conversions.py 88dc65f0117cf7a120f6252674c529e7b9c9b8c3`. It shows 672ca701b3933d930470a7688c86f979c0900bf8 as a rename, 9a8a78d1df3ca96f8d26884b8a08e03a7260c925 as a semantics-preserving refactor from the nested public/owner check to `if conversion_obj and not access.can_see(...)`, and 88dc65f0117cf7a120f6252674c529e7b9c9b8c3 changing that to `if not conversion_obj or not access.can_see(...)`. The latter is the direct closing fix and returns 403 for a missing parent.

At the fix, `website/repos/conversions.py:get` returns None for an inactive conversion unless include_deleted=True, while get_history fetches the ConversionHistory row independently. `website/db_class/db.py:ConversionHistory.to_json` serializes conversion_id, input_text, old_output_text, and new_output_text. `bin/start_website.py` mounts conversions_blueprint at /conversions, establishing the reproducible request path and disclosed fields.

Release boundary: `git tag --contains bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34 --sort=version:refname` prints v1.3, v1.4, v1.5, so v1.2 predates the introducer and v1.3 is the first tagged affected release. `git tag --contains 88dc65f0117cf7a120f6252674c529e7b9c9b8c3 --sort=version:refname` prints only v1.5, so v1.3-v1.4 are affected tagged releases and v1.5 is the first tagged fixed release. The advisory publishes no package version range, so these boundaries are derived from repository ancestry rather than an advisory package claim.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file commit bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34` shows author and committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com> and the exact trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. The commit is a normal one-parent feature commit, parent 3e456f1d952e564965feafd370ab030826cf3f47, not a merge, release, revert, move, or squash aggregate. No PR-body, branch-name, later-refactor, or fix-commit AI signal is used in the verdict.
reasoning: The endpoint was introduced earlier, but at that time normal deletion physically removed the conversion and its history through the foreign-key cascade; the advisory's retained deleted-parent state did not exist. The causal lifecycle changes at bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34: deletion begins retaining inactive conversions and their history, yet the direct history-id reader is not audited or gated. The next commit narrows the broad exposure but explicitly preserves the deleted-parent disclosure by combining a lookup that hides inactive rows with a truthiness-guarded authorization check. Repository migration f5c348eed5a63a6c306cac23b214430adbbffe1f and shared-predicate refactor 9a8a78d1df3ca96f8d26884b8a08e03a7260c925 merely carry the same behavior forward. The direct fix makes missing-parent state deny by default. Because the smallest causal BIC is a normal commit whose commit object explicitly co-credits Claude Sonnet 4.6, and its soft-delete lifecycle change is the root cause that made sensitive history survive without updating its reader, the closed verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
